acceptance_criteria.given: A user visits the site for the first time with their OS set to Dark Mode
acceptance_criteria.then: The site displays in Dark Mode without a visible flash of Light Mode.

acceptance_criteria.given: A user has previously selected 'Light Mode'
acceptance_criteria.then: The site remains in Light Mode.
acceptance_criteria.when: The user refreshes the page or navigates to a new route

acceptance_criteria.given: The user is on any page of the site
acceptance_criteria.then: The theme switches immediately and the new preference is saved.
acceptance_criteria.when: The user clicks the theme toggle

assumptions.assumption: The site uses standard Tailwind CSS 'class' strategy for dark mode.
LocalStorage is an acceptable persistence mechanism for a sandbox site.

clarified_description: Implement a theme switching mechanism (Light/Dark mode) for the Pixie sandbox Next.js site. The system must detect the user's operating system preference on the initial visit, allow users to manually toggle between light and dark modes, and persist that preference across sessions and page refreshes using local storage. To ensure a high-quality user experience, the implementation must prevent the 'flash of unstyled content' (FOUC) where the wrong theme is visible during page load.

constraints.detail: Theme detection must occur in a blocking manner in the document head to prevent the 'flash' effect (FOUC).
Must leverage existing Tailwind CSS configuration for dark mode support.

must: Provide a visible toggle to switch between light and dark modes.
Persist the user's theme choice in `localStorage`.
Respect the user's operating system (prefers-color-scheme) preference on the first visit if no manual choice exists.
Ensure the theme is applied before the page content renders to prevent a 'flash' of the wrong theme.
The toggle must be accessible from every page on the site.
rationale:
The core requirement is preventing the flash of unstyled content (FOUC), which is a common pitfall in Next.js/SSR applications. This necessitates a client-side script in the `<head>` to execute before hydration. We are prioritizing the 'must' requirements of persistence and OS preference to meet the user's definition of success.

## Memory writes
- DECISION: Use `localStorage` for theme persistence to avoid backend complexity in a sandbox environment.
- DECISION: Implement a blocking script in the document `<head>` to prevent theme flashing (FOUC).
- CONSTRAINT: Theme implementation must utilize existing Tailwind CSS dark mode classes.
should: Use an icon-based toggle (e.g., Sun/Moon) for visual clarity.
Incorporate smooth CSS transitions for theme switching if performance allows.
wont: The system will not sync theme preferences across different devices or browsers (no backend/account-based persistence).
The system will not introduce a new design system; it will use existing Tailwind CSS dark mode utilities.
